editorial.headline: Other Shrub Fruit Farming, With Bali Still Open to PMA
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01259 covers integrated farming of other shrub fruit plants, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01259 is a narrow agricultural classification for other shrub fruit farming. Its Indonesian scope points to the cultivation of other shrub plants, including locust beans, and treats the activity as an integrated farming chain rather than a single isolated step. The work begins with land preparation and nursery or seed activities, continues through sowing, planting, and crop maintenance, and extends to harvesting and post-harvest work when those activities are carried out as one continuous operation.

That matters because the code is not simply about trading fruit, running a farm-adjacent service, or processing a commodity after it has left the field. The record describes a production activity rooted in the cultivation cycle itself: preparing the land, establishing the plants, maintaining them, taking the harvest, and handling the immediate post-harvest stage as part of the same agricultural sequence. For founders, the clean reading is that this code belongs to operators whose business identity is the farming of other shrub fruit plants, including locust beans, not a downstream or unrelated commercial activity.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it is not confined to a single enterprise size in the slim record. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is equally clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a stated foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain English, the national classification allows foreign ownership up to the full recorded ceiling for this activity. There is no lower cap in the record to soften or reinterpret; the relevant source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali reading is also unusually clean. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance: for this record, the activity is nationally foreign-open and, on the Bali moratorium fields provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.
